answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a yarrow as the anchor of the cost.
